correctness.rationale: The elementary symmetric-difference identity reduces the eighteen-vertex graph identification definition to 171 explicit hitting constraints. C++ tests all 262144 labelled subsets, proving no code of size 0..6 and exactly 90 of size 7. Independently Python builds actual closed-neighborhood landmark signatures on all 63004 candidates of size at most seven. Both test every one-vertex exchange among 90 optima and agree on 81 edges, nine copies each of bowtie, three-path and edge. Python additionally enumerates and checks six dihedral orbits and all adjacency actions. Both embedded checkers were compiled/run or executed successfully. No finite count was inferred from a sample.

value.rationale: Nine is the first complete repeat block singled out by the nine-column construction in arXiv:1507.05083v1. The exact census and exchange decomposition answer a natural placement-mobility question: optimizing the number of sensors does not permit free movement between solutions. Three distinct component motifs and six symmetry orbits are structural information beyond a routine re-evaluation of the known seven-code construction. This is an exact, self-contained finite fact with a plausible use as a benchmark for reconfiguration algorithms; no unsupported downstream general theorem is claimed.
